subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose stripInboundMetadata for channel plugins

question: Should OpenClaw expose the current inbound metadata sanitizer as a public plugin SDK subpath, and which helper names/subpath should become the supported contract?
rationale: The code need is clear, but adding a plugin SDK helper is a durable public API and security boundary decision that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Approve a narrow sanitizer subpath
options.body: Expose `stripInboundMetadata` and, if desired, `hasInboundMetadataSentinel` from a focused SDK subpath with docs, export metadata, API baseline, and sanitizer/export tests.

options.title: Defer to trusted decoration work
options.body: Wait for the broader trusted inbound-decoration contract before blessing the text-sentinel sanitizer for external plugins.

options.title: Keep sanitizer internal
options.body: Reject an SDK export and require external channel plugins to own their own delivery sanitization despite copy/drift risk.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow sanitizer subpath
recommendation.body: Expose `stripInboundMetadata` and, if desired, `hasInboundMetadataSentinel` from a focused SDK subpath with docs, export metadata, API baseline, and sanitizer/export tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current checkout attributes the sanitizer/export metadata carrier commit to this person, making them the best available routing owner for the API/security shape decision.
